brief: A shelf unit rated to hold 50 kg of books, with two drawers.

requirements.evidence: Built a small hex shelf unit: full bases piece:0,0,0, piece:1,0,0, piece:0,1,0 and piece:0,0,1 (level 1), with two full-depth 2-compartment bins bin:0,1,0 and bin:1,0,0 as book cells, closed with caps and joint bolts. check_build is ok with meshClash clear. No book props were placed: the compartments are too small for the book props in this layout, so the books are not shown.

requirements.requirement: Rated to hold 50 kg of books
requirements.evidence: The configurator checks fit and collisions only; it does not model load, strength or rating. I cannot verify a 50 kg capacity, and the printed material and print quality are not something I can see. Nothing in the build establishes this rating.
Two drawer frames in notches: hex-drawer-frame-notch-mf at notch (-1,1,0) and at notch (1,1,0), between the base cells. The drawers were added and the build passes check_build.

finish.summary: I built a small hex shelf unit with two drawer frames and two book bins, and it passes check_build with meshClash clear. The 50 kg rating is unmet: the configurator does not model load, and I cannot verify it from the printed plastic. The shelf is for books, but I did not add book props because they did not fit the bin compartments.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
